name: WhatsApp
tagline: Encrypted messaging and calls tied to your phone number, used by roughly everyone.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Personal use is free; the paid side is the WhatsApp Business Platform, billed per conversation.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely build a chat app in an afternoon. What you cannot build is the two billion people already on the other end of it, which is the entire product. WhatsApp's value is that your landlord, your aunt, and the plumber are all reachable at a phone number you already have, with delivery that works on bad networks and cheap phones. Self-hosted messengers die the moment you have to ask someone to install something. The honest consolation prize is a private group chat for people who already like you enough to install your thing.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted group chat server with web clients, accounts you create by hand, real-time messages over WebSockets, and message history in SQLite.
requirements: A small always-on server or VPS with a domain and TLS
Everyone you want to talk to willing to install or bookmark your thing
Accepting no push notifications on iOS unless you go native
whatYouLose: Everyone. The contact graph is the product.
Phone number identity, so no contact-book discovery and no 'just text me'
Push notifications that actually wake a sleeping phone
Battle-tested end-to-end encryption, media compression, and delivery on terrible networks
Voice and video calls, voice notes, status, groups of a thousand people, backup and restore
moatNotes: The phone number as identity is the quiet part: it bootstrapped the graph off the address book you already had, and it is also why leaving is so expensive.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody pays for personal WhatsApp, which is exactly the problem: the price of the alternative is not money, it is convincing dozens of people to change how they reach you. Businesses pay through the Business Platform because that is where the humans are, not because the API is good. Any replacement competes against free, ubiquitous, and preinstalled on half the planet's phones. That is not a feature gap you code around.
notes: A chat app is a weekend; a chat app other people open is not. The moat is the phone number as identity plus the address book it was bootstrapped from, which means every contact you have is a switching cost.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted private group chat for a small circle, under 20 people. This is a consolation build, not a WhatsApp clone: no phone numbers, no discovery, no federation.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Node 20 with TypeScript, Fastify for HTTP, ws for WebSockets
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/chat.db
- Vanilla TypeScript frontend bundled with Vite, no React
- Everything in one repo, one npm run dev to start server and client

In scope:
- Rooms table, messages table, users table. Users are created by a CLI script: npm run adduser -- name password. No signup, no email, no password reset.
- Login with password, session cookie signed with SESSION_SECRET from .env, httpOnly, SameSite strict
- WebSocket per connected client, authenticated from the session cookie. Broadcast new messages to everyone in the room.
- Message history: last 200 messages loaded on room open, infinite scroll upward paginated by id
- Typing indicators and online presence, both in memory only, lost on restart
- Image and file upload to ./data/uploads, 10MB cap, served behind the session check, original filename sanitized
- Markdown-free plain text rendering with strict HTML escaping, plus clickable links
- Mobile-first CSS, installable as a PWA with a manifest and a service worker that caches the shell only

Explicitly out of scope, do not build:
- End-to-end encryption. Say so plainly in the README: messages are plaintext in SQLite and TLS is your only transport protection.
- Push notifications, voice or video calls, read receipts, reactions, threads, federation, SMS

Deliver: README with setup, .env.example with SESSION_SECRET and PORT, a Caddyfile for TLS in front, a systemd unit, and a backup.sh that tars data/. No telemetry, no analytics, no third-party scripts.
